app.title: Tashwish: Gulf GNSS Interference Observatory
app.lede: Maps and event evidence for GNSS jamming-like and spoofing-like behaviour inferred from public aircraft broadcast (ADS-B) data. Not for navigation or safety of life. Nothing here is attributed to any actor. Every number links to its method. Cells with too little data or no receiver coverage are shown separately and are never drawn as quiet.

events.heading: Events
events.help: Sort with the column buttons. Choose an event to see its evidence and jump to its first bucket. Read spoofing-like events with care: a position jump seen by only 3 aircraft can be a data error or a multilateration (MLAT) artefact rather than a real event. The implied speed is what the position jump would mean if it were movement; it is not a physical speed.

validation.title: Validation
validation.lede: Not for navigation or safety of life. No attribution to any actor. The numbers below come from the results folder and are never typed by hand. Each row says whether it is a SYNTHETIC test (invented scenarios added to real traffic) or an OBSERVED test (real held out days). Failures are reported with the successes.
validation.empty: This release has no validation results. Until they exist, no claim about detection quality should be made.
validation.synthetic_note: These numbers belong to the SYNTHETIC SAMPLE and say nothing about the real system.
validation.caption: Validation results
validation.limits: Injected synthetic interference and replayed incidents are weak tests of a real system. See the methodology index for how each number is computed.

regime.heading: What happened to the data on 2 March
regime.body: The first {n_before} days of this dataset look alike: about {air_before} aircraft per day and a median en route degraded share of {sh_before}. From {break_day} the picture changes: about {air_after} aircraft per day and a median degraded share of {sh_after}. This is the largest feature of the data, so read every other view with it in mind.
regime.nocause: No cause has been identified, and nothing is attributed to any actor. The change could reflect real interference, a change in the receiver network, a change in air traffic, or a mix of these. Detection results are therefore reported separately for normal and reduced traffic days on the validation page.

validation.group_syn_p: The scenarios are invented and added to real traffic. These rows measure whether the detector finds what was put in. They are not accuracy against real interference.
validation.group_obs_h: Tests on real held out days (OBSERVED)
validation.group_obs_p: These rows are computed from real days that were not used to fit the baseline.
validation.misses: The misses are listed with the hits in docs/research/PREDICTIONS_RESULTS.md in the repository.

vrow.false_coverage_rate: Share of cells that the coverage model called covered but that had too few aircraft on a real held out day.

baselines.lede: The system is set against simple detectors on the same injected scenarios and on the same real days. Where a simple detector matches the system on a row, the extra machinery has not shown a gain on that row. Intervals are 95% day bootstrap intervals. The system row is marked.
baselines.regime_label: Traffic regime for the recall tables
baselines.split_dev_p: The system was developed on these days. The simple detectors were not tuned on any day.
baselines.split_held_h: Held out days (post hoc, not preregistered)
baselines.split_held_p: These days were kept out of fitting the baseline. The comparison on them is post hoc, not preregistered.
baselines.syn_p: Higher is better. The scenarios are invented and added to real traffic, so this measures whether a detector finds what was put in, not accuracy against real interference.
baselines.syn_cap: Recall of the system and simple detectors on injected scenarios, {split}
baselines.obs_h: Flagged cell buckets per day on real days
baselines.obs_p: Burden, not error: there is no ground truth for real days. A flagged cell bucket is not claimed to be a false alarm or a true event. Fewer flags means less to review and says nothing about being right.
baselines.obs_cap: Flagged cell buckets per day on real days, {split}
baselines.obs_spoof_h: Spoofing-like flags per day: origin units of position jumps
baselines.obs_spoof_cap: Flagged origin units per day on real days, {split}
baselines.col_spoof: Spoofing recall, 3 or more aircraft displaced
